_doc: Every confirmed carrier of the 'Will of D.' in canon. LADDERED (2026-08-22): each carrier is a stack of rungs; a reader sees the highest rung their Spoiler Shield cutoff has earned. The gate is when the reader learns the D. IS in the name -- not the character's debut: Law debuts at 498 but 'Trafalgar D. Water Law' is a Ch. 763 reveal, so he is absent from this page for 265 chapters of readers who know him well. Status is part of the rung (Ace is 'active' until Ch. 574). Hints and speculation entries carry their own chapters; speculation about a character is itself a leak of that character. page_min: below Ch. 154 (Kureha names 'the Will of D.') the page shows only a sealed notice.

rungs.text: Protagonist. The D. sits in his name from the very first chapter -- what it means, he neither knows nor cares.
Protagonist. Awakened the Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika -- the Sun God fruit. The D. and the Dawn keep pointing at the same man.
The Marine who cornered Roger, over and over.
Vice Admiral. Cornered Roger. Luffy's grandfather.
Leader of the Revolutionary Army. Luffy's father. Origin unrevealed.
Whitebeard's Second Division Commander. Luffy's big brother, hunting a traitor from his own division.
Born Gol D. Ace -- Roger's son, carried 20 months by Portgas D. Rouge to hide him. He took his mother's name.
Born Gol D. Ace; took his mother's surname Portgas. Killed at Marineford shielding Luffy.
Ace's mother. Held her pregnancy 20 months by sheer will to protect Ace from the Government's hunt.
The Pirate King's true name -- 'Gold Roger' was a corruption. Conquered the Grand Line; executed at Loguetown with a smile.
First and only Pirate King. Reached the final island, learned the truth of the Void Century, and named the island Laugh Tale. Executed at Loguetown.
The traitor of Whitebeard's Second Division -- the man Ace hunts. Preached about dreams at Mock Town and meant every word.
Betrayed Whitebeard twice over: took the Yami Yami no Mi, then took the dying Whitebeard's Gura Gura no Mi. The only known holder of two Devil Fruits.
Yonko. Holds two Devil Fruits (Yami Yami + Gura Gura). Theorised to be more than one person.
Worst Generation Supernova and Ope Ope no Mi user. Survived Flevance's Amber Lead disease; Corazon died keeping the D. in his name a secret.
Former Vice Admiral. Saved baby Robin from the Buster Call on Ohara, and was frozen by Aokiji for it.
Former Vice Admiral who saved baby Robin from the Buster Call. Aokiji's ice did not kill him -- he lives, and he saved Ohara's books too.
Captain of the Rocks Pirates (Whitebeard, Big Mom, Kaidou, Shiki). Killed at God Valley by Roger and Garp together.

_canon_hints.text: Dr. Kureha, watching Chopper sail away: 'the Will of D. lives on.' The first time anyone names it as a thing that survives its carriers.
Whitebeard, dying at Marineford: 'One Piece is real.' The implication is that the D. carriers are the ones destined to inherit Roger's will.
Corazon told Law the stories: in some lands the D. clan are called 'the natural enemy of the gods' -- and the gods, in this world, wear the Government's crest.
Roger and Whitebeard both spoke of it: the D. carriers will start a great war that will engulf the world.
Common readings of the D.: 'Doom' (death-bringers to the Celestial Dragons), 'Dawn' (those who herald a new age), or simply the family marker of a lineage the world was made to forget.

_speculation.text: Imu -- long theorised to bear the D. (Nerona D. Imu). The family name 'Nerona' is canon; the D. status is fan-deduction from the D. clan's opposition to the World Government. Not yet confirmed.
Loki and Harald (Elbaph) -- Sun God / Joy Boy connections in the Elbaph arc have prompted D. theories. Not yet confirmed.
Yamato -- sometimes theorised to be a hidden D. via Kaidou's lineage. Not confirmed.
Shanks -- fan theory based on his secrecy and his standing with the world's highest powers. Not confirmed.
